title: In larval zebrafish, a single-neuron projectome predicts region-level trial-residual coupling beyond distance and region effects, but not stimulus-locked coupling (25 regions, 11 fish)
abstract: Question: does the anatomical projectome of the larval zebrafish brain predict which region pairs have correlated activity, and is the prediction specific to the pair? Approach: we registered 4,426 mapzebrain single-neuron tracings to the Z-Brain space of whole-brain light-sheet calcium data from 11 larvae (Chen et al. 2018). We made a structural score S for 1,225 pairs of 50 region-hemisphere nodes and regressed functional coupling (FC) on a distance spline, hemisphere flags and node fixed effects. We used edge-permutation and region-label nulls, per-fish fits, split-half reliability and five structural specifications. Findings: S and FC correlate (r = 0.45), but distance and region effects explain most of this link. For whole recordings with the primary score, the pair-specific partial r was 0.02 (p = 0.67), although residual FC (reliability 0.90) and residual S (0.79) are reliable; with other structural definitions it was 0.11 (p < 0.04). In five fish with stimulus trials, trial-residual (noise) FC had a positive pair-specific link to S in every fish and every specification (partial r 0.10 to 0.19; OMR p = 0.003, PT p = 0.014), while stimulus-locked (signal) FC had none (-0.04 to 0.07). High-pass filtering alone did not change the link. Limitations: only five fish for condition contrasts, so the noise-minus-signal difference is not significant at the fish level (minimum possible p = 0.0625); coarse regions; tracings have no axon or dendrite labels; atlas registration is approximate.

display.caption: Pair-specific partial correlation between projectome score and FC (distance and node covariates) in five fish. Orange: trial-residual (noise) FC; aqua: stimulus-locked (signal) FC; blue: total FC. Bars: group FC; dots: single fish; grey: 95% edge-permutation null; p: region-label null.

Whole recordings, 11 fish. Left: zero-order relation of projectome score and FC, coloured by distance. Middle: residuals after distance and node effects. Right: partial r for two covariate designs and two FC variants.
Group partial r over five structural specifications. Filled markers: p < 0.05. Noise FC links are positive in all specifications; signal FC links are near zero.
